_about: Zaxxon, ported by The Duplicators, (c) 1984 Sega. A .COM that
relocates twice: the code runs at CS + 0x20, and the data segment is
patched into an immediate at load time to sit 0x5200 bytes further
on -- past the end of the 20,736-byte file.
So the address space is split in two, and the split is the point.
Anything the program reads is `[cs:...]` and is in the image;
anything it writes is `[...]` and is in memory the file never
described. Keys below carry a `cs:` prefix when they mean the first,
and annotate.py learned to tell them apart for this game.
All 74 call targets are named, and so are the scene, boss and wall
handlers the three jump tables reach. Six of the eight names this
file had before were wrong in the same way ParaTrooper's were: taken
from how many callers a routine had.

0x0000: pushes CS+0x20 and returns far into it, after patching the data segment into the immediate at file 0x101
0x0100: sets DS = SS = the patched segment, installs the INT 1Ch handler through the vector at 0:0x70, probes the joystick, and falls into main
0x014C: mode 4 and two INT 10h AH=0Bh palette calls
0x015E: 0x2000 words of zero into ES. It was called port_write
0x0169: CX vertical retraces off port 0x3DA; nothing in the code region reaches it
0x017D: spins on INT 1Ah until the low byte of the tick count changes
0x018C: adds AL to the current player's eight-digit score with AAA, carrying by hand, and sets score_dirty. It was called scene_update
0x01CA: one digit and its carry flag
0x01DD: eight digits, leading zeros dropped by scanning for the first non-zero
0x001EB: walks the eight digits, skipping leading zeros
0x001F7: the inner loop once the first non-zero has been found
0x020C: walks a display script: an attribute byte, a cursor word, a NUL-terminated string, and 0xFF to stop. It was called level_step
0x0222: the string half of that, at cursor DX
0x0233: INT 10h AH=2 then AH=9 with the attribute in text_attr -- BIOS character output on a mode 4 screen
0x0247: counts the discharge on both axes of port 0x201; carry means no stick is attached
0x026F: INT 16h AH=1 then AH=0; returns with ZF if nothing was waiting
0x027C: DI up to CX with AL, in the data segment
0x0286: CX bytes from CS:SI to DS:DI -- how every table in the image reaches a variable
0x0291: the INT 1Ch handler. Samples the joystick into joystick_pos if one is attached, then services the four sound channels
0x02C0: title screen, attract loop, two-player turn taking, high score. The outer loop the game never leaves
0x002C6: the title screen and the attract round, repeated until somebody chooses
0x0330: one player's turn: build the playfield, then the frame loop -- controls, objects, scroll, fuel, collision -- until the ship is lost
0x045E: one more life once the score's fourth digit reaches 2
0x047F: one frame of the death animation, run twenty times with two sprite variants
0x04B4: 0x80 across the whole tile map: every cell empty and every cell dirty
0x04CA: compares eight digits and slides the entry in if it beats them
0x04EE: 0xB4 ticks of waiting for '1', '2', or a joystick button; carry means somebody chose
0x0534: the stage number as two digits at cursor 0x1725, from the third word of the player's context
0x0545: copies a 34 x 22 block of tiles over the map -- the ground the round opens on
0x05BA: the back buffer to the screen: 68 bytes a row, 176 rows, the two CGA banks alternating
0x05D9: returns BX pointing at this player's six-word context in the image -- score, cursor, lives, stage script position. Thirteen routines call it, which is why it was called draw_cell
0x0600: CX ticks. It was called draw_row
0x0608: prints both scores, both lives counts, and whose turn it is
0x0641: the ship icon once per remaining life
0x0682: 16 rows of three words ORed into video with the bank swap in DX
0x06A6: 'Keyboard Control=K' / 'Joystick Control=J', or the refusal if no stick answered the probe
0x0848: jumps through stage_script at the position this player's context holds. It was called dispatcher
0x08B4: rounds the script position down to an entry and reports whether it is one of the two that begin a stage
0x08DD: advances the script by one word, wrapping at the 0xFFFF terminator
0x08FC: the entry every stage script alternates with: world_x down, world_y up, redraw the ship, feed the map
0x0946: writes the ship and its shadow into the tile map as the world scrolls under them
0x0A6B: the first stage: 1000-point bonus, then the wall
0x0AA3: the space stage: state 0 clears the section, 1 points level_tiles at 0x932, 2 unpacks 0x3A5F with mode 1
0x0ADD: each of these seven sets a level pointer, a stage handler, and a scene kind, then unpacks its level
0x0AED: one of seven scenes with the same three-step shape: a stage_handler at 0x3AB1, a scene name pointer, a scene_kind, then unpack_level
0x00B51: steps the stage, reads the handler out of the scene's table, and unpacks its level. Seven scenes jump here
0x00B5F: the same without the handler, for the two scenes that set their own
0x00B84: level_tiles to 0x902 and the default level
0x0B8D: the run-length decoder: 0xFD count value, 0xFE skip, 0xFF finish the row, anything under 0xFC literal. 18 rows of 24 cells into the section bitmap
0x0C1E: one cell of that, eight rows at stride 48
0x0C31: clears the screen, prints '1000 Point BONUS', scores it twice, and resets the scroll
0x0C8C: the clip test; an object outside the window is marked 0xFF, which frees its slot
0x0CC3: picks the bitmap and the blitter for the object's kind out of sprite_table and calls it
0x0CF0: 24 rows of three words, AND the mask at +0x90 then OR the image
0x0D0F: 16 rows of two words, ORed, starting 0x140 into the buffer
0x0D2B: 16 rows of three words, ORed, starting 0x141 -- the odd byte is the half-cell shift
0x0D99: 8 rows of one word, ORed, starting 0x282
0x0DC7: AND only -- how a shadow darkens what is under it
0x0DE3: kinds 0xF0 and up: a frame from explosion_frames, mask and image kept in two separate tables that each wrap on themselves
0x0E31: walks the visible 34 x 22 of the tile map; bit 0x80 means the cell changed, so draw it and clear the bit
0x0E60: eight rows of a word at stride 0x50
0x0E65: the same at stride 0x30, into the section bitmap
0x0E82: straight to video, four double rows with the bank toggled by XOR 0x2000
0x0EB0: copies a rectangle out of the image into the back buffer, clipped on all four sides; the rectangle is the four words at BX
0x0FF0: draws the 29 objects back to front, sorting by depth as it goes, then the ship, then the six slots the wall uses
0x1071: adds each object's velocity, chosen from velocity_table by the low three bits of its second byte
0x1098: clip, blit, then mark the nine or sixteen map cells it covered dirty
0x1110: blocks until the keyboard buffer is empty again
0x1120: silence, clear the sound state, and wait for a second Escape
0x113C: the sample the timer interrupt left in joystick_pos, less the centre reading, clamped to 0..7 on each axis and folded to one of nine directions through joystick_dir_map
0x119C: +0x10, floor at 0, ceiling at 0x1F, then two right shifts
0x11B0: the arrow keys 0x47..0x51 through key_dir_map; space sets fire_pressed
0x11EE: one direction, one move. Clamps X to 6..0x2E and Y to the altitude-dependent band, tracks the shadow, finds a free bullet slot when fire is held
0x13B7: copies the ship's starting state and a full fuel gauge out of the image
0x13E5: the gauge, one tile per cell
0x13FF: draws the altimeter, then burns a cell of fuel every fuel_timer ticks. An empty gauge returns carry, and that is one of the ways the round ends
0x14ED: what a bullet destroyed: a fuel drum refills the gauge, everything else scores through score_table
0x155F: one off the lives byte the player's context points at, with nine frames of grace before it counts
0x1580: reads the current stage's spawn list six ticks at a time and drops each entry into the first free object slot
0x173E: gives the two enemy-shot slots a target: the player's position now, or led ahead of it, depending on what kind of enemy is shooting
0x1843: the fortress: its own small script through boss_script
0x1860: the fortress arrives: six bytes copied over object slot 0xCA once it is free
0x1882: up to five shots from the fortress, one per free slot in the first five, each seeded from boss_shot
0x18E5: waits until all six of the first object slots are free again
0x18F9: resets the scene name to 0x1E15 and steps the stage script
0x1902: the wall between stages, dispatched through wall_script
0x192D: the wall approaches: world_y up to 0x18, and the six wall pieces walk one cell a frame
0x1981: holds for wall_timer frames, then clears bit 7 of draw_flags
0x19A4: did the ship pass: enemy_shots empty and wall_cleared decides whether the script skips a step
0x19C4: world_x back up to 0x57 and world_y down, with the objects hidden
0x19E3: the wall goes: six pieces restored from wall_objects, the section bitmap filled with 0x5555, then twenty frames of the ordinary loop
0x1A6E: '200 Point BONUS' or '2000 Point BONUS' by whether the gap was found, then rebuild the playfield
0x1B03: loads the wall's scroll state, its six objects and its level, and steps the script
0x1BA7: keeps the ship's shadow on the ground under it while the world scrolls
0x1DC5: the ship against all fourteen hazards, then each of the six bullets against all of them. A hit on the ship returns carry and ends the round
0x1E88: a bullet in the fortress: 0x36 of them finishes it
0x1EA3: three units in X, three in Y, and for the kinds that have one, three in altitude
0x1EE9: whether the ship is lined up with the gap
0x1F15: depth 0x14 to 0x1E and altitude 4 or under. One of the seven predicates a scene installs in stage_handler; collisions reaches them all through `call word [9]`
0x1F38: the shared window: depth 0x0E to 0x1E, altitude ignored. Three of the others start by calling it
0x1F55: the inverted one: depth over 0x18 or altitude under 0xC passes
0x1F65: clc -- the shared success tail of all seven
0x1F96: an object's position relative to world_x
0x1F9F: engine_timer to 0x28 -- a short hum rather than silence
0x1FAD: the engine hum: while engine_timer runs, a fresh random divisor every call. It was called hud_update
0x1FD1: four channels at sound_channels; the first active one dispatches through sound_handler
0x2012: channel 1: di 0x35C, eighteen steps, then speaker_stop
0x2034: channel 2: di 0x33FE over 0xB4 steps, halving the rate while sound_variant is set
0x2063: channel 3: di 0x4B0 over four steps, each 0xFFC4 further on
0x02096: the divisor step and the countdown all three channel routines end on
0x209D: clears bit 1 of port 0x61 and leaves bit 0 alone
0x20A4: port 0x43 mode 0xB6, the divisor to 0x42, gate on at 0x61
0x20B7: CX bytes of CH at BX
0x20BD: folds the INT 1Ah tick count into rng_state and returns it modulo 0x51

0x0000: bit 0x0F the player count, 0x10 whose turn, 0x20 a joystick answered the probe, 0x40 the control choice is made
0x0001: set by score_add, tested by the frame loop
0x0002: the attribute put_char passes to INT 10h AH=9
0x0003: the reading taken before the game started
0x0004: the second axis of the reading taken before the game started
0x0006: the image address of the tile set the current scene draws from
0x0008: bit 0 vertical, bit 1 horizontal -- which way the stick was pushed this frame
0x0009: called indirectly by collisions; each scene installs its own
0x000B: 0, 1, 3 or 5, set by each scene and read by the drawing
0x000C: the script word the current stage came from; two values mean the crash animation is skipped
0x000E: the byte the first player's context points at
0x0016: set when the ship went through the gap
0x001F: the fifth word of player 1's context, cleared with the score at the start of a game
0x00FC: the second enemy shot's, tested so two shots never aim at the same column
0x0191: the code offset start puts in the INT 1Ch vector; the same address as timer_isr
0x0201: PSP:0x201 is the immediate of the `mov ax, imm16` at file 0x101. The relocation stub writes the data segment into it before jumping, which is why the listing shows a constant that is never the value the game runs with
0x0021: set to 1 whenever engine_timer is reloaded to 0x64
0x0025: four two-byte channels; bit 0 of each means playing
0x0027: the second of the four two-byte channels at sound_channels
0x0033: read by sound_explosion, which halves its step while it is set
0x0038: the last INT 1Ah reading random took
0x003B: counts down; zero silences the engine
0x003E: six ticks between entries of the spawn list
0x003F: set by the space bar, cleared when it is used
0x0040: 0x14 while the wall holds its position
0x0055: written by the timer interrupt, read by read_joystick_dir -- the one variable two contexts share
0x0057: 16 cells; tile 0x55 is full, and the cell reaching 0x5D empties it
0x0066: how many are left; zero ends the round
0x0067: 0x14 between burns in the air, 3 on the ground
0x0068: 0x80 flying over the fortress, 1 in space
0x0069: the joystick buttons as of the previous frame
0x006A: walks the current stage's spawn list
0x006C: set once the playfield is built and cleared while a stage is changing
0x006E: bit 0 the wall is up, bit 7 it is being drawn
0x006F: set during the wall retreat, when the objects must not be drawn
0x0070: the scroll position; every stage script drives it
0x0072: and its companion, moving the other way
0x00A0: kind, spare, x, y, altitude, spare -- the same six-byte shape as every object
0x00A3: clamped to the band 0x28..0x3E offset by ship_alt
0x00A4: 0 to 0x14; the altimeter and the Y clamp both read it
0x00A6: the object slot the shadow occupies, 0xFF when there is nothing under the ship
0x00A8: the shadow's, set to the ship's position plus (8, -8) when something is under it
0x00AC: 29 slots of six bytes: kind, velocity index, x, y, altitude, damage. 0xFF in the first byte frees the slot
0x00F4: the two slots at index 8 and 9 that enemy_fire fills
0x00F6: the first enemy shot's column, tested so two shots never aim at the same one
0x0100: six slots from index 14; ship_control claims the first free one
0x0136: six slots from index 23, used only while the wall is on screen
0x018A: 16,000 bytes, 200 rows of 80. Object coordinates are 160 bytes to a Y unit, so a Y unit is two scan lines
0x0910: 24 rows down and six bytes in -- where blit_playfield starts reading
0x478A: 6,912 bytes, 48 wide and 144 tall: the unpacked scenery the scroll slides across
0x62B2: 40 x 25 cells. Bit 0x80 is the dirty flag, so a cell of 0x80 is an empty cell that still needs clearing
0x632D: the 34 x 22 of it that map_render walks
cs:0x04E8: score, cursor, stage number, script position, lives, spare

_note: File offsets, contiguous from 0 to the end. Zaxxon has no data
segment in the file at all, so these spans cover the whole image
and the split between code and table is the only division there
The last span is half the file. It earns its single line: nothing
reaches it except tile_table, sprite_table and explosion_frames,
and all three end exactly where the bitmaps they index begin.
0x0000: the far jump and the loader's banner
0x0100: the primitives: video, timing, score, text, input
0x046B: start_map, and the code that copies it
0x05BA: the playfield blit, player context, turn handling
0x0848: the stage script and the scroll
0x0A02: the two scenery patches map_feed stamps
0x0A62: the scenes, the level decoder, the bonus
0x0FF5: the object loops and the two input maps
0x13A7: the fuel gauge, the altimeter, the score table
0x14ED: hits, lives, and the spawn tables
0x1602: the eight spawn lists, one per stage
0x1AE2: the bonus messages, the shadow, and every collision test
0x1F12: the sound channels and the random number generator
0x279B: the sprite bitmaps, their masks, and the explosion frames -- 10,597 bytes, half the file, reached only through those two tables

_note: 18 bracketed constants in the listing are displacements, not
addresses: each appears only with a base register and never on its own,
and every one is under 0x400 -- a field inside a record the base points
at. They are listed so the coverage number has a denominator that means
something, and so the next reader does not go looking for a variable.

_not_addresses: 0x3311 is not an address. It is two bytes of joystick_dir_map -- the 34-byte
table at cs:0x107C that folds two stick axes into one of nine directions --
and the run it sits in decodes cleanly enough that comrec emits it as
`mov byte [bx + si + 0x3311], cl` twice. NASM re-emits the same bytes, so the
rebuild is unaffected, and naming it would invent a variable the game does
The tell is the one knowledge/13 records: referenced from a run with no
incoming branch, and nothing writes it that anything reads.
